signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD outperforms all G10 peers over 1W with an average gain of +1.101% across 4 pairs, while JPY anchors the bottom at -0.689% across 7 pairs, opening an extreme 1.790% leader-to-laggard divergence. The structural divergence is backed by cash carry, where RBA at 4.60% against BoJ at 1.25% yields a +335bp nominal policy spread and a +337bp AONIA-TONA overnight advantage favoring AUD. AUD/JPY trades at 110.769, comfortably absorbing broader market noise as carry demand maintains upward pressure. However, CFTC JPY net short positioning sits stretched at -37,820 contracts (88th percentile), leaving the cross vulnerable to violent squeezes if volatility broadens. Trade bias: Long AUD/JPY, backed by dominant +337bp OIS carry. Catalyst: Japan Adjusted Trade Balance at 23:50 UTC. Risk: VIX breaking above 20 triggers rapid carry-trade liquidation.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.17, holding between its 20-day SMA at 157.97 and 200-day SMA at 158.56. Escalating maritime disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz following reports of a damaged supertanker layer supply-shock tension over the pair. Saxo 1M 25-delta risk reversals print at -1.93, indicating an acute put skew as institutional desks actively purchase downside USD/JPY protection. This heavy options hedging conflicts with CFTC speculative positioning, where leveraged funds remain heavily short JPY at -37,820 contracts (88th percentile). While the 265bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage keeps spot underpinned, the 160.00 threshold marks the pivotal zone where official intervention sensitivity escalates sharply. Trade bias: Neutral/short USD/JPY, pressured by extreme options put skew and geopolitical headline risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct. Risk: Spot breaking cleanly above 160.00 without official resistance.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1240, positioned beneath its entire moving average complex with SMA20 at 1.1274, SMA50 at 1.1465, and SMA200 at 1.1585. Leveraged funds hold an extreme net short position of -92,833 contracts, sitting at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of -1.78. Saxo 1M options show implied volatility elevated at 6.6% against a 4.1% 30-day realized volatility, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +2.4%. Meanwhile, Fed policy at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp carry advantage supporting USD and limiting sustainable upside rallies. The heavy institutional short posture creates asymmetric squeeze exposure if technical resistance gives way. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by negative carry and moving-average resistance. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct. Risk: Daily close above the 20-day SMA at 1.1274 triggering forced short covering.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Hawkish CB Divergence + Resistance Test
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3380, clearing its 20-day SMA at 1.3249 and testing the overhead technical cluster formed by the 50-day SMA at 1.3414 and 200-day SMA at 1.3434. Multiple hawkish interventions from BoE official Greene emphasize that UK monetary policy remains insufficiently restrictive against ongoing inflation persistence. This hawkish push contrasts with Fed policy pricing ahead of next week's FOMC, narrowing the policy divergence as UK 2Y yields trade at a 5bp premium to US equivalents. Leveraged funds hold modest net long positioning of +13,065 contracts (21st percentile), reflecting room for institutional accumulation if inflation metrics surprise to the upside. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD, driven by hawkish BoE rhetoric and short-term moving average support. Catalyst: UK CPI release at 06:00 UTC. Risk: UK headline CPI missing the 2.7% consensus, invalidating the hawkish policy thesis.
